claim: FoF1-ATP synthase is a ubiquitous enzyme that synthesizes or hydrolyzes ATP coupled with proton translocation at the inner mitochondrial membrane, chloroplast thylakoid membrane, and bacterial plasma membrane.
source: FoF1-ATP synthase (FoF1) is a ubiquitous enzyme that synthesizes or hydrolyzes ATP coupled with proton translocation at the inner mitochondrial membrane, chloroplast thylakoid membrane, and bacterial plasma membrane (Boyer, 1997; Walker, 2013; Yoshida et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published works (Boyer, 1997; Walker, 2013; Yoshida et al., 2001) that establish this as known scientific knowledge.

claim: FoF1 synthesizes ATP via rotation of the central rotor driven by the proton motive force across the membrane.
source: FoF1 synthesizes ATP via rotation of the central rotor driven by the proton motive force across the membrane.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the mechanism of FoF1-ATP synthase.

claim: The FoF1 enzyme comprises two rotary motors that share the rotor: the water soluble F1, which has catalytic sites for ATP synthesis/hydrolysis, and the membrane-embedded Fo, which mediates proton translocation.
source: The enzyme comprises two rotary motors that share the rotor, that is, the water soluble F1, which has catalytic sites for ATP synthesis/hydrolysis (Noji et al., 2017), and the membrane-embedded Fo, which mediates proton translocation (Kühlbrandt, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published works (Noji et al., 2017; Kühlbrandt, 2019) describing the structure and function of FoF1.

claim: The Fo motor consists of a c oligomer ring (c-ring), which serves as the rotor, and the ab2 stator portion located on the c-ring periphery.
source: The Fo motor consists of a c oligomer ring (c-ring), which serves as the rotor, and the ab2 stator portion located on the c-ring periphery.
evidence: This describes the structural composition of the Fo motor based on established knowledge.

claim: Downgradient proton translocation through Fo drives rotation of the central rotor composed of a c-ring and γε subunits, thereby inducing conformational changes in F1 that result in ATP synthesis.
source: Downgradient proton translocation through Fo drives rotation of the central rotor composed of a c-ring and γε subunits, thereby inducing conformational changes in F1 that result in ATP synthesis.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of ATP synthesis based on established knowledge of FoF1 function.

claim: ATP hydrolysis in F1 induces reverse rotation of the rotor, which forces Fo to pump protons in the reverse direction.
source: Conversely, ATP hydrolysis in F1 induces reverse rotation of the rotor, which forces Fo to pump protons in the reverse direction.
evidence: This describes the reverse operation of FoF1 based on established knowledge.

claim: The c-ring is composed of 8–17 c-subunits depending on the species.
source: The c-ring is composed of 8–17 c-subunits depending on the species (Watt et al., 2010; Stock et al., 1999; Mitome et al., 2004; Meier et al., 2005; Matthies et al., 2009; Vollmar et al., 2009; Pogoryelov et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations documenting the variable stoichiometry of c-subunits across species.

claim: FoF1 from thermophilic Bacillus PS3 and yeast mitochondrial FoF1 contain 10 c-subunits in the c-ring, which is designated the c10-ring.
source: FoF1 from thermophilic Bacillus PS3 and yeast mitochondrial FoF1 contain 10 c-subunits in the c-ring, which is designated the c10-ring (Stock et al., 1999; Mitome et al., 2004; Symersky et al., 2012; Guo et al., 2019; Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published works and reference to Figure 1 showing the structure.

claim: The Fo-c subunit harbors an essential proton-binding carboxyl group (c-Glu; cE56 in Bacillus PS3, cE59 in yeast mitochondria) located near the center of the membrane-embedded region; this group functions as the proton carrier.
source: The Fo-c subunit harbors an essential proton-binding carboxyl group (c-Glu; cE56 in Bacillus PS3, cE59 in yeast mitochondria) located near the center of the membrane-embedded region; this group functions as the proton carrier (Figure 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1a showing the location of these residues.

claim: Protonation in the Glu allows the c10-ring to bind a proton, whereas proton release leads to Glu deprotonation.
source: Protonation in the Glu allows the c10-ring to bind a proton, whereas proton release leads to Glu deprotonation.
evidence: This describes the protonation mechanism based on established knowledge of the proton carrier function.

claim: Bacterial FoF1 activity is significantly decreased when the corresponding key residue is modified by the inhibitor N,N-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (DCCD).
source: Accordingly, bacterial FoF1 activity is significantly decreased when the corresponding key residue is modified by the inhibitor N,N-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (DCCD) (Hermolin and Fillingame, 1989) or mutated to other amino acids (Dmitriev et al., 1995)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Hermolin and Fillingame, 1989.

claim: Bacterial FoF1 activity is significantly decreased when the corresponding key residue is mutated to other amino acids.
source: Accordingly, bacterial FoF1 activity is significantly decreased when the corresponding key residue is modified by the inhibitor N,N-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (DCCD) (Hermolin and Fillingame, 1989) or mutated to other amino acids (Dmitriev et al., 1995)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Dmitriev et al., 1995.

claim: Bacillus PS3 FoF1 carrying a single cE56Q mutation in the c10-ring does not catalyze ATP-driven proton pumping or ATP synthesis.
source: and Bacillus PS3 FoF1 carrying a single cE56Q mutation in the c10-ring does not catalyze ATP-driven proton pumping or ATP synthesis (Mitome et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Mitome et al., 2004.

claim: The a-subunit comprises two separate half-channels, one connecting the c-ring to the periplasm side of the bacteria or the intermembrane space side of the mitochondria, the other connecting the c-ring to the cytoplasmic side of the bacteria or the matrix side of the mitochondria.
source: The a-subunit comprises two separate half-channels, one connecting the c-ring to the periplasm side of the bacteria or the intermembrane space side of the mitochondria, the other connecting the c-ring to the cytoplasmic side of the bacteria or the matrix side of the mitochondria (Figure 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1b showing the schematic of the half-channels.

claim: Recent cryo-electron microscopy (EM) structural analyses of FoF1 at near-atomic resolution have revealed two long tilted parallel α-helices in the a-subunit at the interface with the c10-ring.
source: Recent cryo-electron microscopy (EM) structural analyses of FoF1 at near-atomic resolution (Allegretti et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015) have revealed two long tilted parallel α-helices in the a-subunit at the interface with the c10-ring.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to cryo-EM structural studies (Allegretti et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015).

claim: An essential Arg residue (aR169 in Bacillus PS3, aR176 in yeast mitochondria) at the middle of the long parallel helices plays a critical role in separating the two half-channels by preventing proton leakage.
source: An essential Arg residue (aR169 in Bacillus PS3, aR176 in yeast mitochondria) at the middle of the long parallel helices plays a critical role in separating the two half-channels by preventing proton leakage (Mitome et al., 2010)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Mitome et al., 2010.

claim: In the half-channels, two highly conserved Glu residues (aE223 and aE162 in yeast mitochondria) are regarded as proton-relaying sites.
source: and in the half-channels, two highly conserved Glu residues (aE223 and aE162 in yeast mitochondria) are regarded as proton-relaying sites (Srivastava et al., 2018; Figure 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Srivastava et al., 2018 and reference to Figure 1a.

claim: The attractive interaction between a-Arg and deprotonated c-Glu is hypothesized to contribute to Fo rotation.
source: Since the essential Arg (a-Arg) localizes near c-Glu in the c10-ring, the attractive interaction between a-Arg and deprotonated c-Glu is hypothesized to also contribute to Fo rotation (Vik and Antonio, 1994).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Vik and Antonio, 1994.

claim: In Fo rotation models proposed based on experimental studies, the c-subunits facing the a-subunit perform three functions (proton release, electrostatic interaction with a-Arg, and proton uptake) depending on their positions relative to the a-subunit.
source: In the Fo rotation models proposed based on experimental studies (Vik and Antonio, 1994; Elston et al., 1998; Kubo et al., 2020), the c-subunits facing the a-subunit perform three functions (proton release, electrostatic interaction with a-Arg, and proton uptake) depending on their positions relative to the a-subunit.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to experimental studies (Vik and Antonio, 1994; Elston et al., 1998; Kubo et al., 2020).

claim: A high-resolution structure analysis of yeast mitochondrial FoF1 showed four of the 10 c-subunits to be facing the a-subunit.
source: A high-resolution structure analysis of yeast mitochondrial FoF1 showed four of the 10 c-subunits to be facing the a-subunit (Srivastava et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Srivastava et al., 2018.

claim: Three key residues, that is, aGlu162, aR173, and aGlu223, localize between the c-Glu residues of the four c-subunits, suggesting that the c-Glu residues of adjacent c-subunits could cooperate through the a-subunit residues.
source: Three key residues, that is, aGlu162, aR173, and aGlu223, localize between the c-Glu residues of the four c-subunits, suggesting that the c-Glu residues of adjacent c-subunits could cooperate through the a-subunit residues.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural observations about the spatial arrangement of key residues.

source: A more recent theoretical study using a hybrid Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics (MC/MD) simulation based on a high-resolution structure showed that there can be two or three deprotonated c-Glu residues facing the a-subunit concurrently (Kubo et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a computational study (Kubo et al., 2020).

claim: The waiting time for protonation of c-subunits is shared among two or three c-subunits.
source: This suggests that the waiting time for protonation of c-subunits is shared among two or three c-subunits.

source: FoF1 mutants carrying one or two cE56D substitutions in the c10-ring were expressed in host Escherichia coli cell membranes at approximately one-tenth the level of wild-type (WT) FoF1.
